elicitation_input.question: What are the differences between the different birth control devices that actually exist?
elicitation_input.question_type: Open-ended question that is potentially ambiguous

llm_generation.text:
# Birth Control Methods: A Comprehensive Comparison

## Hormonal Methods

**Combined Oral Contraceptives (The Pill)**
- Contains estrogen and progestin
- Approximately 91% effective with typical use, about 99% effective with perfect use
- Failure rate roughly 7-9% per year in typical use
- Requires daily dosing at roughly the same time
- Common doses: ethinyl estradiol ranging from about 10-35 micrograms combined with various progestins

**Progestin-Only Pills (Mini-Pill)**
- Around 91% effective with typical use
- Must be taken within a strict 3-hour window daily
- Often used for breastfeeding mothers or those who can't take estrogen

**Contraceptive Patch (Xulane, Twirla)**
- About 91-93% effective with typical use
- Applied weekly for 3 weeks, then one week off
- Delivers roughly 150 mcg norelgestromin and 35 mcg ethinyl estradiol daily
- May be slightly less effective in people over approximately 198 lbs (90 kg)

**Vaginal Ring (NuvaRing, Annovera)**
- Approximately 91-93% effective with typical use
- NuvaRing: replaced every 3-5 weeks
- Annovera: reusable for up to 1 year (13 cycles)

**Depo-Provera (Injection)**
- About 94% effective with typical use, roughly 99.8% with perfect timing
- Injected every 12-13 weeks
- Contains 150 mg medroxyprogesterone acetate
- Can cause delayed return to fertility (average 9-10 months after stopping)

**Contraceptive Implant (Nexplanon)**
- Over 99% effective (one of the most effective reversible methods)
- Failure rate less than 0.1% per year
- Lasts approximately 3-5 years
- Small rod (about 4 cm long) inserted under the skin of the upper arm
- Releases roughly 68 mg etonogestrel

## Intrauterine Devices (IUDs)

**Hormonal IUDs**
- Mirena: effective for about 8 years, releases roughly 20 mcg levonorgestrel daily initially
- Kyleena: lasts approximately 5 years, smaller size
- Liletta: effective for about 8 years
- Skyla: lasts around 3 years, smallest hormonal IUD
- All over 99% effective; failure rates around 0.1-0.4%

**Copper IUD (Paragard)**
- Non-hormonal
- Effective for up to 10-12 years
- Over 99% effective (failure rate about 0.8%)
- Can be used as emergency contraception if inserted within 5 days of unprotected sex

## Barrier Methods

**Male Condoms**
- About 82-87% effective with typical use, 98% with perfect use
- No hormones; latex, polyurethane, or polyisoprene materials
- Only method providing significant STI protection

**Female/Internal Condoms**
- Roughly 79
